source_title: PM Modi Slams Opposition in Banaskantha Over Anarchy, Launches Rs 14,400-Crore Projects - India Today - India Today
source_excerpt:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched development projects worth approximately 14,400 crore rupees in Banaskantha, Gujarat, reflecting on his 25-year political journey from the state. In his address, he launched a sharp attack against the opposition, accusing them of spreading fake narratives about shortages of gas and urea amid global supply disruptions caused by the US-Iran conflict. He stated that these narratives were designed to gain control and spread anarchy across the country. Modi affirmed that the government ensured uninterrupted urea supplies at existing rates and resolved to serve the public until his last breath, with plans to announce an additional 19,000 crore rupees under the PM-Kisan scheme. MSP, Solar Pumps and Dairy Sector: Boost for Farmers Across India
A public address detailed government initiatives supporting farmers and transforming the rural economy across the country. Amid rising global fertiliser costs, nearly 16 lakh crore rupees were spent to shield agriculturalists from price spikes, alongside distributing over 24 lakh crore rupees under minimum support price schemes for wheat and paddy over the last twelve years. More than two lakh crore rupees have been disbursed under the PM Fasal Bima Yojana, while around 12 lakh solar pumps sanctioned under the PM-KUSUM scheme saved over 80 crore litres of diesel. Science and technology have also been introduced into daily farming, with 26 crore Soil Health Cards and nearly 3,000 climate-resilient seed varieties distributed. Furthermore, dairy and animal husbandry sectors received significant support through the Rashtriya Gokul Mission, free vaccination drives administering nearly 150 crore doses, and scientific breeding techniques, boosting average daily milk output from under five litres in 2013-14 to nearly eight litres.
Supreme Court Cancels Anand Singh's Bail, Sets December 1 Surrender Deadline
In a major setback to expelled Janata Dal (United) legislator Anand Singh, the Supreme Court has directed him to surrender by December 1. Singh, an accused in the 2025 Dulare Chand Yadav murder case, had earlier been granted bail by the Patna High Court. That decision was challenged before the top court through a petition seeking the cancellation of his bail. The Supreme Court rejected relief for the Mokama legislator, setting an ultimatum for him to return to custody by the stipulated deadline while further details of the order are awaited.
Amit Shah Chairs Key UP BJP Huddle In Lucknow To Chalk Out 2027 Poll Strategy
Union Home Minister Amit Shah chaired a major Bharatiya Janata Party election meeting in Lucknow alongside Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the deputy chief ministers, and senior party leaders. The huddle focused on formulating a roadmap for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections following the recent Legislative Council poll results, including the Varanasi seat. Key challenges discussed among the cadre include tackling growing anti-incumbency after a decade in power and formulating an effective strategy to counter the Samajwadi Party's PDA campaign led by Akhilesh Yadav ahead of the upcoming electoral contest.
SC Cancels Bail Of Expelled JDU MLA Anand Singh In Dularchand Yadav Murder Case
The Supreme Court has delivered a major setback to expelled Janata Dal (United) legislator Anand Singh by cancelling his bail in connection with the Dularchand Yadav murder case. Hearing a petition challenging the relief granted to the Mokama legislator by the Patna High Court, the apex court directed Singh to surrender before authorities by December 1. The order sets aside the earlier bail granted by the High Court.
